items.title: Bitcoin plunges to lowest since 2024 amid global tech sell-off

featured_image.name: Bitcoin drops 15%, briefly breaking below $61,000 as sell-off intensifies, doubts about crypto grow

items.description:
Bitcoin plunged to its lowest level since 2024 and Asian equity markets mostly declined on Friday as a punishing sell-off in technology stocks on Wall Street reverberated across global markets.

The world's largest cryptocurrency dropped below $64,000 on Thursday, briefly touching $60,062, in what analysts described as the worst single-day drop since the FTX collapse in November 2022. The cryptocurrency has now fallen roughly 50% from its October 2025 peak near $126,000.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Webb detects methyl radical outside Milky Way for first time

featured_image.name: James Webb telescope reveals molecular origins of planetary ...

items.description: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has achieved a remarkable trio of discoveries in recent weeks, producing the highest-resolution map of dark matter ever created, confirming the most distant galaxy ever observed, and detecting an unprecedented richness of organic molecules in a nearby galaxy's hidden core.

items.title: Global stocks tumble as tech selloff triggers Korean trading halt

featured_image.name: Dow tumbles nearly 600 points, S&P 500 goes negative for 2026 in tech sector rout: Live updates

items.description:
Global markets tumbled Thursday as a brutal selloff in U.S. technology shares extended into a third consecutive day, sending the S&P 500 into negative territory for 2026 and dragging Bitcoin to levels not seen in more than a year.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 593 points, or 1.2%, while the S&P 500 also fell 1.2%. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.6%, marking its worst two-day decline since tariff-related turmoil last April, according to The Wall Street Journal. In Asian trading Friday, the selloff continued, with South Korea's Kospi triggering a brief trading halt after plunging more than 5%.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Bitcoin drops below $61,000, down 50% from October peak

featured_image.name: Bitcoin briefly breaks below $61,000 as sell-off intensifies - CNBC

items.description:
Bitcoin experienced its worst single-day decline in over three years on Thursday, briefly falling below $61,000 as a punishing selloff in technology stocks spilled into cryptocurrency markets and erased trillions of dollars from digital asset valuations.

The world's largest cryptocurrency touched a low of approximately $60,062 during late trading before recovering slightly to trade around $62,500 by evening, according to CNBC and CoinGecko data. The roughly 15% daily drop marks the steepest one-day decline since November 2022 and leaves Bitcoin more than 50% below its record high of $126,080 reached just four months ago in October 2025.[1][2][3]

items.title: 2026 Winter Olympics open with Alps blanketed in artificial snow

featured_image.name: Italian expert's manufactured snow will play big role at the ...

items.description:
The 2026 Milan-Cortina Winter Olympics, which officially begin on February 6 with a historic dual-location opening ceremony, will depend almost entirely on manufactured snow as warming temperatures and unpredictable natural snowfall reshape the future of winter sports in the Alps.

Organizers have deployed approximately 2.4 million cubic meters of artificial snow across competition venues—equivalent to twice the volume of Rome's Colosseum—requiring roughly 948,000 cubic meters of water and 125 snow cannons to prepare courses for elite athletes.[1][2]

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 4.6 amid Super Bowl ad clash

featured_image.name: Sam Altman Slams Anthropic Super Bowl Ads Jabbing OpenAI's Ad ...

items.description:
Anthropic and OpenAI are sharpening their competitive edge in a battle for AI supremacy, with both companies unveiling new enterprise products this week while exchanging barbs over dueling Super Bowl advertisements. The public spat between the two startups—whose origins intertwine from OpenAI's own ranks—signals a pivotal moment as both companies race to prove they can build sustainable businesses from their costly AI ventures.

On Wednesday, Anthropic released a series of television ads set to air during Super Bowl LX that mock OpenAI's decision to introduce advertisements into ChatGPT. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman responded on X, calling the spots "funny" but "clearly dishonest," accusing Anthropic of "doublespeak." The commercials feature the tagline "Ads coming to AI. But not to Claude" and depict humorous scenarios where an ad-supported chatbot derails user requests with intrusive product placements.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Italy enacts decree allowing police to detain protesters before demonstrations

featured_image.name: Italians Protest US Plans to Deploy ICE at Winter Olympics ...

items.description:
The Italian government on Thursday enacted a sweeping security decree granting police new powers to detain suspected troublemakers for up to 12 hours before public demonstrations, a measure that civil liberties groups condemned as an assault on constitutional rights. The decree came just one day before planned protests at the opening ceremony of the Milano Cortina Winter Olympics.

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's cabinet approved the legislation following violent clashes in Turin last weekend, where more than 100 police officers were injured during a demonstration against the closure of the Askatasuna social center, according to the interior ministry. Video footage showed masked protesters attacking an officer with kicks, punches, and hammer blows.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Ukraine and Russia swap 314 prisoners in first exchange in months

featured_image.name: Ukraine and Russia carry out first prisoner exchange in months as U.S. touts "tangible results" in peace talks

items.description:
Ukraine and Russia conducted their first prisoner exchange in five months on Thursday, swapping 157 captives each following two days of US-mediated peace talks in Abu Dhabi that ended without resolving the war's core disputes over territory and ceasefire terms.

The swap brought home 150 Ukrainian military personnel and seven civilians, with most having been held since 2022, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Ukraine's Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War. Among those freed were 19 Ukrainians who had been illegally sentenced by Russian courts, including 15 serving life imprisonment, Ukrainian intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov confirmed. The youngest released prisoner is 23 years old, having been captured at age 19 during the defense of Mariupol.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: British scientists unveil AI that tracks icebergs from birth to breakup

featured_image.name: Antarctic iceberg the size of Chicago breaks off, reveals ...

items.description:
Scientists at the British Antarctic Survey have unveiled an artificial intelligence system capable of tracking icebergs throughout their entire lifecycle, from the moment they break off from glaciers to their eventual disintegration in open waters, the organization announced Thursday.

The AI tool addresses what researchers have described as a "major blind spot" in climate science by creating detailed "family trees" that link fragmented iceberg pieces back to their original parent formations, something that has not previously been possible at scale.

items.title: Venezuela passes first vote on amnesty for political prisoners

featured_image.name: Venezuela’s National Assembly approves amnesty bill in first of two votes

items.description: Venezuela's National Assembly unanimously approved the first reading of an amnesty bill on Thursday that could lead to the release of hundreds of political prisoners and pave the way for exiled opposition figures to return home. The legislation represents the most sweeping reform effort since acting President Delcy Rodríguez assumed power following the U.S. military capture of Nicolás Maduro last month.

items.title: Ginkgo Bioworks, OpenAI cut protein costs 40% with GPT-5 lab

featured_image.name: How Ginkgo Bioworks leverages synthetic biology to shape ...

items.description:
Ginkgo Bioworks and OpenAI announced today that their collaboration using a GPT-5-powered autonomous laboratory achieved a 40 percent reduction in cell-free protein synthesis costs, marking a milestone in the application of artificial intelligence to biological research. The biotechnology company reported the system reduced the cost of producing superfolder green fluorescent protein from $698 per gram to $422 per gram over six months of testing.[1][2][3]

The announcement, detailed in a scientific preprint not yet peer-reviewed, describes how the autonomous lab executed more than 36,000 experiments across six iterative cycles and generated nearly 150,000 data points with minimal human involvement. Human roles were primarily limited to reagent preparation, loading and unloading materials, and system oversight, while the AI managed experimental design, execution, data interpretation, and hypothesis generation.[2][4][5][3]

items.title: Study links COVID lockdowns to record methane surge

featured_image.name: COVID-19 Shutdowns Lead to Cleaner Air | AQMD Seeks to ...

items.description:
The pandemic measures that cleared city streets and grounded airplanes created an unexpected consequence: they weakened the atmosphere's ability to scrub away methane, helping to trigger the largest recorded surge in the potent greenhouse gas, according to a new study published in the journal Science.

A team of 41 scientists led by researchers at Peking University found that reductions in hydroxyl radicals during the COVID-19 period from 2020 to 2021, followed by a recovery through 2023, accounted for roughly 80 percent of the interannual variations in methane's growth rate.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump backs UK Chagos deal after reversing earlier criticism

featured_image.name: UK, US agree Chagos air base is of strategic importance after Trump criticism of deal

items.description:
President Donald Trump signaled support on Thursday for Britain's controversial agreement to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius, reversing his previous sharp criticism of the deal while warning he retains the right to "militarily secure" the strategically vital Diego Garcia airbase.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump said he understood the agreement negotiated by Prime Minister Keir Starmer was "the best he could make," according to Reuters. The statement marks a dramatic turnaround from his January remarks when he labeled the same deal "an act of great stupidity" and "total weakness".[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Trump endorses Japan's Takaichi ahead of Sunday election

featured_image.name: Japan's snap elections: A reckless risk or calculated gamble?

items.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump threw his support behind Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Thursday, days before Japan's snap legislative election, and confirmed that the Japanese leader will visit the White House on March 19.

In a message posted on Truth Social, Trump called Takaichi "a strong, powerful, and wise Leader" who "truly loves her Country," giving what he described as his "Complete and Total Endorsement" of her and her governing coalition ahead of Sunday's vote.[1][2]

"Prime Minister Takaichi is someone who deserves powerful recognition for the job she and her Coalition are doing," Trump wrote, concluding with the all-caps rallying cry: "SHE WILL NOT LET THE PEOPLE OF JAPAN DOWN! Good luck on your very important Sunday Vote".[3]

items.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to exchange 314 prisoners at Abu Dhabi talks

featured_image.name: Russia and Ukraine agree new prisoner exchange after talks

items.description:
Delegations from the United States, Ukraine, and Russia reached an agreement on Thursday to exchange 314 prisoners of war, marking the first such exchange in five months and a tangible outcome from ongoing peace negotiations in Abu Dhabi.

US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff announced the deal on social media platform X, stating that "this outcome was achieved from peace talks that have been detailed and productive." He added that "while significant work remains, steps like this demonstrate that sustained diplomatic engagement is delivering tangible results and advancing efforts to end the war in Ukraine."[1][2]

Witkoff expressed gratitude to the United Arab Emirates for hosting the discussions and credited President Donald Trump for his leadership in making the agreement possible. The exchange represents the first prisoner swap between Moscow and Kyiv since October 2025.[3][4][1]

items.title: Black hole emits energy a trillion times greater than Death Star

featured_image.name: Black hole burps up shredded star years after consuming it ...

items.description:
A supermassive black hole has been "burping out" the remains of a shredded star for four years and is still ramping up, with scientists predicting its radio emissions will continue growing until reaching a peak in 2027.

The phenomenon, described as potentially one of the most powerful single events ever detected in the universe, has released energy estimated to be at least a trillion times greater than the fictional Death Star—and possibly closer to 100 trillion times that figure, according to research published Wednesday in the Astrophysical Journal.[1][2]

items.title: New START treaty expires as Russia shadows European satellites

featured_image.name: European Commission confirms Russia targets EU satellites and ...

items.description:
Two Russian spacecraft have intercepted communications from at least a dozen key European satellites over the past three years, European security officials told the Financial Times, as the last remaining nuclear arms control treaty between the United States and Russia expired on Wednesday.

The dual developments mark a concerning escalation in space-based tensions and the collapse of decades of nuclear restraint between the world's two largest atomic powers.

items.title: US and Russia reach informal deal as New START treaty expires

featured_image.name: Explainer: Could US and Russia extend last nuclear weapons treaty?

items.description:
UN Secretary-General António Guterres on Wednesday urged the United States and Russia to negotiate a new nuclear arms control framework "without delay" as the New START treaty expired at midnight, warning that the world now faces the highest risk of nuclear weapons use "in decades."[1][2][3]

The expiration of the 2010 agreement—which capped both nations' deployed strategic nuclear warheads at 1,550 and established verification mechanisms—marks what Guterres called "a grave moment for international peace and security." For the first time in more than 50 years, no binding limits exist on the strategic nuclear arsenals of the two nations that together possess roughly 87% of the world's nuclear weapons.[2][4][5][1]

items.title: Xi urges Trump to handle Taiwan arms sales 'with prudence'

featured_image.name: China's Xi reasserts Taiwan stance in call with Trump, while U.S. ...

items.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping urged President Donald Trump to handle arms sales to Taiwan "with prudence" during a phone call on Wednesday, February 4, underscoring Beijing's view that the Taiwan issue remains "the most important issue" in U.S.-China relations. The exchange, the first direct conversation between the two leaders since November, came as both sides prepared for Trump's planned April visit to Beijing.[1][2]

items.title: Wargame finds Russia could seize Lithuanian city in days

featured_image.name: Wargame simulates how Russia could take Nato country 'within days'

items.description: A tabletop military exercise conducted by former German and NATO officials in December 2025 concluded that Russia could capture the strategically vital Lithuanian city of Marijampole within days by exploiting allied indecision rather than overwhelming force. The findings, published this week, have intensified scrutiny of NATO's decision-making capabilities and political resolve in a potential crisis.
